analysis: The changed file is documentation only (docs/architecture/inference.md): a date bump, a KV re-slice floor note near head line 985, a cluster-service health-file paragraph (head ~3532-3540) and later cluster-runtime edits. The two supplied units (head lines 2465-3234) are unchanged context and carry no changed ranges from the file_changes map, so I found no diff-introduced content in them. I read them against the threat model. They cover template render checks, a typed 400 for unsupported reasoning effort, vision and media caps, MiMo native ownership, cluster registration, and the pair-cluster data plane. Nothing in them changes a control or invalidates a threat assumption. The text states fail-closed behavior consistently: media caps, pre-allocation checks, typed refusals, no peer-supplied environment in owner launch, and load-agreement binding of lane counts. No source or security code is modified, so no regression is evident. Two items were not verifiable from the supplied evidence. First, the new health-file paragraph (a supervisor liveness guard accepting only the service's own PID, and a separate part-health.json) lies outside the supplied units, so its code is not reviewed. Second, the cluster data plane (an encrypted, authenticated JACCL link) is described only in prose, and the threat model does not define a cluster trust boundary. The cluster and distributed material may warrant a threat-model entry, but that is a documentation-scope question and not a finding from this PR. The doc/code consistency of the health-file PID check (ClusterServiceAgent.healthPath) should be checked by whichever pass sees the code.
